Mechanistically, 3'UTR lengthening reduced NF-YA protein expression through decreased mRNA stability, impaired translation, and enhanced nuclear retention, rather than increased miRNA-mediated repression. Enforced NFYA 3'UTR lengthening in PCa cells via CRISPR/Cas9 or ASOs diminished NF-YA protein levels and suppressed aggressive tumor traits both in vitro and in vivo. These findings establish NFYA APA as a critical determinant of NF-YA oncogenic output and downstream tumor-promoting programs, and as a previously unrecognized driver of PCa progression. Importantly, they provide proof-of-concept for gene-specific, APA-directed therapeutic strategies. ASO-mediated modulation of polyadenylation indeed emerges as a clinically translatable approach to fine-tune oncogene expression, thus opening new avenues for RNA-based precision interventions in aggressive PCa.

title: Triphenyl phosphate promotes gastric cancer progression via LDHA deubiquitination-induced lactate production and H3K18 lactylation.
abstract: Triphenyl phosphate (TPP) is an organophosphate flame retardant widely detected in environmental matrices and human tissues. Although its endocrine-disrupting effects are well-documented, the role of TPP in gastric cancer (GC) progression remains to be elucidated. The effects of TPP on the proliferation, migration, and invasion of MKN-28 and MKN-45 cells were evaluated. A nude mouse xenograft model was employed to assess the tumor-promoting effects of TPP in vivo. Ubiquitination assays and cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays were performed to examine LDHA protein stability. Furthermore, integrated RNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses were utilized to identify downstream transcriptional programs and signaling pathways. TPP exposure significantly promoted the proliferation, migration, and invasion of GC cells in vitro and accelerated tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, TPP treatment increased LDHA protein levels through suppressed protein degradation rather than enhanced transcription. The reduction in LDHA ubiquitination induced by TPP was associated with altered expression of APOL3 and NDRG1, suggesting that these regulators may mediate the effect of TPP. The accompanying lactate accumulation was associated with a significant increase in histone H3K18la levels. Integrated epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses suggested that H3K18la enrichment is linked to the activation of oncogenic programs, including the WNT/β-catenin, Notch, and hypoxia signaling pathways. The present study suggests that TPP exposure contributes to malignant phenotypes in GC, likely via an APOL3/NDRG1-LDHA regulatory pathway that promotes lactate accumulation and H3K18la-associated transcriptional reprogramming. These findings implicate TPP as a potential environmental risk factor for GC and provide experimental evidence supporting further investigation of this metabolic-epigenetic axis in cancer intervention.

title: Herbaceous intercropping reshapes soil microbial communities and induces transcriptomic responses in Morchella.
abstract: Morchella cultivation faces challenges from continuous cropping obstacles, which are often linked to soil degradation and microbial community shifts. Intercropping has emerged as a potential strategy to mitigate these constraints, yet the ecological mechanisms underlying herbaceous companion plant effects on Morchella remain poorly understood. This study investigated how intercropping with two functionally distinct herbaceous species-Poa pratensis and Vicia sativa-affects Morchella growth, soil microbial assembly, and Morchella transcriptional responses. Three cultivation treatments were established: Morchella monoculture (CK), intercropping with P. pratensis (B), and intercropping with V. sativa (P). Soil physicochemical properties, microbial community composition (16 S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequencing), and Morchella fruiting body transcriptomes (RNA-seq) were analyzed. Intercropping reduced Morchella yield by 23.7% (P treatment) to 36.9% (B treatment) compared with monoculture, yet significantly increased soil available potassium and promoted companion plant growth. Microbial community analysis revealed that intercropping decreased the relative abundance of Ascomycota, particularly Morchella itself (reduced to approximately one-quarter of control levels), while increasing fungal α-diversity and enriching taxa such as Mortierella and Rhizopus. Bacterial communities also shifted, with Pseudomonas abundance increasing 3.3-fold (B) and 3.8-fold (P). Transcriptomic analysis identified 572 upregulated DEGs in the B treatment and 1,090 in the P treatment. Commonly upregulated DEGs were enriched in GO terms related to monocarboxylic acid metabolism, iron ion transport, and carbohydrate binding, and in KEGG pathways including fructose and mannose metabolism and nitrogen metabolism. Treatment-specific responses included enrichment of oxidation-reduction processes in B and symbiont attachment and biofilm formation in P. Continuously upregulated DEGs across the CK-B-P gradient were associated with chromatin assembly and metabolic pathway activation. Herbaceous intercropping reconfigures the Morchella cultivation system by altering soil nutrient availability, reshaping microbial community structure, and inducing adaptive transcriptional responses in the fungus. Although intercropping enhanced soil ecological conditions and microbial functional diversity, it did not translate into yield improvement, suggesting ecological trade-offs between resource competition and environmental optimization. These findings provide a foundation for understanding host-microbe-plant interactions in fungal cultivation systems and highlight the need to balance ecological benefits with productivity outcomes.

title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand-receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

title: Identification of immune- and cellular senescence-related genes in keloids through integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveKeloids are pathological scars resulting from abnormal connective tissue growth in the skin. Although cellular senescence has been implicated in fibrotic diseases, its role and molecular characteristics in keloids remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify cellular senescence-related genes associated with keloid pathogenesis and investigate their potential relationships with alterations in the immune microenvironment.MethodsPublicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE44270 and GSE92566) and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (GSE181297) from the Gene Expression Omnibus database were integrated for analysis. Cellular senescence-related genes were obtained from the CellAge database and intersected with differentially expressed genes identified between keloid and normal samples to obtain cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes. Protein-protein interaction network analysis was performed to identify hub genes, which were further intersected with single-cell differentially expressed genes to determine key genes. Immune infiltration was assessed using the Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts algorithm, and cellular senescence-associated biological pathways were evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and gene set variation analysis. The expression patterns and cellular distribution of key genes were further evaluated using single-cell sequencing data.ResultsA total of 18 cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes were identified between keloid and normal samples. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified 10 hub genes, and integration with single-cell transcriptomic data revealed 5 key genes associated with cellular senescence: cyclin D1, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8, galectin 3, and notch receptor 3. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression between keloid and normal groups across the combined bulk-transcriptomic datasets. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated significant associations between key genes and immune cell characteristics. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A was correlated with gamma delta T cells and resting dendritic cells, whereas notch receptor 3 was associated with CD8+ T cells and naive CD4+ T cells. Single-cell analysis further characterized the expression patterns of key genes across different cell populations in keloid tissues.ConclusionThis study provides an integrated transcriptomic and single-cell landscape of cellular senescence-related alterations in keloids. The identified key genes are associated with cellular senescence-related transcriptional changes and immune microenvironment characteristics in keloid tissues. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression patterns at the bulk-transcriptome level, suggesting their relevance in keloid pathogenesis. These findings highlight the potential involvement of cellular senescence-associated programs in the interplay between fibroblast activation and immune alterations in keloids and provide candidate genes for further functional investigation.

title: Serendipita indica reshapes early metal allocation and root-associated transcriptional responses in Sedum alfredii under combined cadmium-lead stress.
abstract: Mechanistic studies of plant-microbe interactions under heavy metal stress have focused predominantly on single metal exposure, whereas contaminated soils commonly contain multiple metals whose combined effects cannot be predicted directly from responses to individual contaminants. Here, we investigated how the root endophytic fungus Serendipita indica (S. indica) influences metal acquisition, allocation, and root transcriptional responses in the hyperaccumulator Sedum alfredii (S. alfredii) exposed to individual or combined cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) stress. Metal quantification was integrated with RNA sequencing, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and RT-qPCR validation. Under combined stress, S. indica increased root Cd and Pb concentrations, enhanced root-normalized shoot metal accumulation, and promoted root-to-shoot translocation. Combined Cd-Pb exposure elicited a transcriptional response distinct from those induced by either metal alone, while fungal inoculation further reshaped gene expression patterns associated with metal detoxification, redox regulation, protein homeostasis, and energy metabolism. Co-expression analysis identified gene modules associated with fungal inoculation and combined metal exposure, and RT-qPCR supported the RNA-seq expression trends of CSP4, atp2, SPBP35G2.11c, and RPS21. These findings demonstrate that S. indica modifies both metal acquisition and host stress responses under Cd-Pb co-stress, providing mechanistic insight into microbe-assisted phytoremediation of multi-metal-contaminated soils.

title: Multi-Omic Profiling for Molecular Diagnosis of Erythrodermic Skin Diseases.
abstract: Erythroderma is one of the most challenging clinical scenarios in modern dermatology. It represents an acute, potentially life-threatening inflammatory condition characterised by erythema and scaling affecting more than 90% of the skin surface, with mortality rates up to 9%. Various underlying skin diseases cause erythroderma yet are difficult to distinguish clinically and histopathologically. This poses a major diagnostic challenge and delays targeted therapy, with potentially severe acute and long-term consequences. To define disease-specific molecular programs in erythrodermic skin using integrated proteomics and transcriptomics, and to translate these into a diagnostic framework. Here we performed mass spectrometry (MS) - based proteomics and RNA sequencing on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded skin biopsies from 96 patients with erythroderma caused by pityriasis rubra pilaris (PRP, n=19), psoriasis (n=18), atopic dermatitis (AD, n=20), cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL, n=18), drug-induced maculopapular rash (MPR, n=21), and 20 healthy skin controls. Samples from four independent centers were included and MS-based proteomics was acquired on the Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer. We performed multi-omic data integration through multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA), and disease classification was achieved using the adaptive machine-learning framework ADAPT-Mx, benchmarked against blinded clinico-histopathological assessment. We quantified over 9,300 proteins and 17,200 protein-coding transcripts, revealing distinct molecular signatures for each disease. The proteome showed elevated expression of type-2 immunity-associated Charcot-Leyden crystal protein in AD, establishing a potential link between eosinophil-dominant inflammation and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Transcriptomic analysis demonstrated selective upregulation of IL-17C in PRP, correlating strongly with IL-1 family cytokine expression. Notably, only a subset of PRP patients exhibited this signature, suggesting treatment-relevant disease endotypes. Multi-omic integration identified elevated expression of T-cell regulator RASAL3 in CTCL, not previously characterized in its pathogenesis. ADAPT-Mx, our machine-learning classifier, achieved 73.9% diagnostic accuracy in the held-out test cohort, outperforming conventional clinico-histopathological assessment (59.5%), with AUC values of 0.87-1.00 across disease entities. This study provides an integrated multi-omic framework for inflammatory skin diseases, combining RNA sequencing with large-scale MS-based proteomics. By enabling per-sample classification without imputation, our workflow offers proof of concept for multi-omic-driven diagnosis that can support clinical decision-making across inflammatory skin diseases.

title: Application of a Human Nasal Mucosa Ex Vivo Culture System to Model Inflammatory Responses.
abstract: IntroductionThe nasal cavity is the entry point of the upper respiratory tract and the primary site of inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens.MethodsHuman nasal mucosa (HNM) tissues were obtained from patients undergoing endoscopic nasal surgery. Six HNM specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis were used for paired Der p 1 challenge experiments, and 8 chronic rhinosinusitis-derived HNM specimens were used for paired SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points.ResultsCultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. HDM stimulation enhanced secretory activity and induced IL-4 and IL-5 expression at day 3. Both SARS-CoV-2 variants (HU-1 and Omicron BA.2) produced detectable viral RNA and viral N-protein signals in HNM expressing Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 and Transmembrane Protease Serine 2. Viral inoculation induced an interferon-associated antiviral response, which was most pronounced following HU-1 exposure, although between-variant differences in the measured antiviral markers were not significant. At 3 days postinfection under standardized infection conditions, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2 at day 3.DiscussionThe ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, including an intact epithelial barrier, stromal immune cells, and glandular components, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform that complements conventional 2-dimensional cultures. HDM-sensitized HNM showed Der p 1-associated type 2 responses, whereas the viral arm revealed an antiviral response and exploratory variant-associated differences in epithelial injury.ConclusionsShort-term ex vivo HNM may provide a practical tissue-level platform for investigating upper-airway responses to allergen exposure and SARS-CoV-2 infection. It preserves multicellular tissue architecture, while further validation in larger, better-stratified cohorts and extended culture optimization will support broader mechanistic and translational application.

title: Granzyme K associates with inflammatory immune programs and B-cell dysregulation in systemic lupus erythematosus.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterized by systemic immune activation and multi-organ inflammation. Granzyme K (GZMK), a serine protease predominantly expressed by CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells, has emerging non-cytotoxic inflammatory functions, but its relevance to SLE remains incompletely defined. In this study, we conducted investigations using plasma and tissue analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, an animal model, and primary human B cell experiments. Plasma GZMK was increased in patients with SLE and was associated with clinical disease activity. Integrated multi-tissue single cell analysis identified preferential GZMK enrichment in CD8+ effector memory T (Tem) cells and a higher relative abundance of this compartment in SLE, while proteomic profiling and multiplex immunofluorescence provided protein and tissue level evidence for a GZMK-enriched CD8+ memory T cell population. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested enhanced predicted communication between Tem and B lineage cells, and circulating GZMK was further associated with a plasma cell-like population. In two murine models, PPACK, which can inhibit GZMK catalytic activity but is not GZMK selective, attenuated lupus associated inflammatory phenotypes and partially normalized altered splenic B cell composition. In vitro experiments showed that active recombinant GZMK augmented plasma-cell-associated phenotypic and transcriptional responses under B cell expansion conditions. Collectively, these findings identify circulating GZMK as an independent correlate of SLE clinical activity and characterize a recurrent GZMK-enriched CD8+ memory/Tem cell program across peripheral blood and affected tissues that is associated with B-cell dysregulation and plasma-cell-related immune abnormalities.

title: METI-FS: a multi-evidence temporal integration framework for biomarker discovery in small-sample time-series transcriptomics.
abstract: Selecting a small set of experimentally verifiable candidate biomarkers from small-sample, time-series RNA-seq data (n < 50, p > 10,000) remains a critical bottleneck for downstream functional studies. Current approaches suffer from three unresolved limitations: differential expression-based pre-filtering lacks temporal awareness, machine learning-based feature selection lacks automatic sparsity control, and individual analytical steps are not integrated into a coherent end-to-end workflow. We developed METI-FS (Multi-Evidence Temporal Integration for Feature Selection), a multi-evidence integration framework whose principal contribution is temporally aware upstream compression: through the intersection of maSigPro temporal regression, WGCNA co-expression network analysis, and DESeq2-based minimum effect size testing, METI-FS systematically reduces the feature space from p > 10,000 to a high-quality candidate pool containing several hundred to several thousand genes, thereby improving the selection stability of a broad range of downstream machine learning methods. A data-driven gap-union threshold automatically determines the final feature set size with minimal user-specified parameters. Across 210 simulation scenarios encompassing six co-expression architectures, METI-FS achieved a relaxed precision (precision_any) of 0.904, indicating that over 90% of the selected genes carried genuine temporal signal (strict precision: 0.408 ± 0.308; F1: 0.296 ± 0.178). Ablation analysis with full paired comparisons identified maSigPro temporal filtering as the most critical upstream component (ΔF1 = -0.206 ± 0.169). On four cross-domain GEO datasets spanning immune activation, anti-tumor drug response, viral infection, and cartilage inflammation, METI-FS achieved compression ratios ranging from 602:1 to 2722:1 without any parameter adjustment. Across all four datasets, the effect size filter (which tests whether each gene's log₂ fold change statistically exceeds a minimum threshold) removed 14-77% of genes that passed temporal and co-expression filters, demonstrating that statistical significance and biological significance require independent assessment. A two-layer benchmarking framework demonstrated that maSigPro-based upstream filtering improved downstream Boruta selection stability by 65% on average across datasets (mean pairwise Jaccard index: 0.288 to 0.475). Cross-validation against published literature across all four datasets confirmed that 75% (41 of 55) of the candidate genes had independent functional evidence, demonstrating that METI-FS, without any biological prior knowledge, independently converges on genes with established functional roles. METI-FS provides a largely automated end-to-end framework for biomarker discovery in small-sample, time-series transcriptomics. Its core contribution is temporally aware upstream compression that systematically enhances the selection stability of a broad range of downstream methods, coupled with data-driven sparsity control that eliminates manual parameter tuning. The R implementation and all analysis scripts are publicly available at GitHub.

title: Integrative RNA-seq identifies differentially expressed genes and protein targets of titanium dioxide and zinc oxide in Escherichia coli.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria pose a major global health threat, contributing to rising mortality and economic loss despite the extensive use of broad-spectrum and last-resort antibiotics. Escherichia coli is widely used as a model Gram-negative bacterium for investigating antimicrobial stress responses. Although metal oxide nanoparticles (MONPs) exhibit broad antibacterial activity, the molecular responses associated with MONP exposure remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to characterize E. coli responses to MONPs and evaluate YnjC as a candidate MONP-interacting protein. ZnO- and TiO₂-associated transcriptomic datasets showed broad regulation of genes involved in membrane processes, ion transport, oxidative-stress responses, and metabolic pathways. The ynjC gene was prioritized as the top network-derived hub candidate based on convergent Maximal Clique Centrality and MCODE module evidence. Docking and MD analyses compared YnjC interactions with ZnO, TiO₂, and MgO, while apo YnjC provided a structural baseline. The simulations showed material-dependent effects on YnjC dynamics and time-resolved persistence of protein-nanoparticle association. Together, these findings demonstrate similar molecular pathways disrupted by MONP exposure and identify key candidate proteins that unravel their antibacterial mechanisms, providing potential biomarkers and targets for future antimicrobial therapy.
authors: Wan Amirul Syazwan Wan Ahmad Munawar

title: Associations of 6PPD-quinone exposure with macrophage-related LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 signatures in cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is a widespread tire-derived contaminant linked to cardiotoxicity and metabolic dysfunction, but its role in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. Using chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and ischemic heart disease as surrogate models, we combined network toxicology, multi-omics, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify candidate common molecular drivers of 6PPDQ toxicity and CMM pathogenesis. LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 were consistently dysregulated across the three disorders. Docking and MD simulations indicated plausible 6PPDQ binding and relative conformational stability to all three proteins, without confirming actual binding or quantitative affinity ranking. Single-cell RNA-seq of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) showed predominant enrichment of these targets in macrophages, while CellChat predicted disease-associated communication patterns (macrophage-fibroblast in DCM; macrophage-endothelial in DN). Dose-response screening identified 20 ng/mL-an estimated high-exposure dose under heavy pollution-as the peak-effect concentration for target-gene modulation and M1-marker (iNOS, CD80) induction; it was used thereafter, although extrapolation to typical exposure warrants caution. At this concentration, 6PPDQ induced RAW264.7 morphological remodeling, intracellular ROS accumulation, and M1-like polarization, characterized by upregulation of iNOS, CD80, LYN, and SOCS3, repression of TIMP2, and elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings associate 6PPDQ-induced macrophage inflammation and ECM-related changes with coordinated LYN/SOCS3/TIMP2 dysregulation, providing a framework linking 6PPDQ exposure to CMM-related inflammatory-fibrotic signatures.

title: Serum microRNA Landscape in Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Hypothesis-Generating Reference Dataset.
abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an eosinophilic vasculitis arising against a background of adult-onset asthma. We investigated circulating microRNA (miRNA) profiles in EGPA and integrated them with previously reported serum protein data. In this retrospective, cross-sectional study, archived sera from 14 patients with active, glucocorticoid-naïve EGPA and 20 with severe eosinophilic asthma without EGPA were profiled on a 2,588-miRNA microarray. Differential expression among 1,777 quantifiable miRNAs was assessed with limma, adjusting for sex and RNA integrity number; significance required both a Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate below 0.05 and a Bonferroni-corrected p below 0.05. TargetScan-predicted target genes were intersected with 29 serum proteins previously shown to differ between the same groups. Two further paired analyses, each performed in a separate group of patients with EGPA, compared active disease with the glucocorticoid-treated phase (n = 11) and samples before versus after mepolizumab (n = 13). Eight miRNAs met both criteria: hsa-miR-3126-5p, hsa-miR-921, hsa-miR-6836-5p and hsa-miR-668-5p were lower in EGPA, and hsa-miR-6857-3p, hsa-miR-1260a, hsa-miR-603 and hsa-miR-12125 were higher (within-cohort areas under the curve, 0.82-0.94). Fourteen of the 29 proteins were encoded by predicted target genes. Only hsa-miR-3678-3p changed after glucocorticoid treatment; no miRNA changed after mepolizumab, and none of the eight EGPA-associated miRNAs changed with either treatment. This exploratory study identifies circulating miRNA differences between EGPA and severe eosinophilic asthma, and the complete result table is provided as a reference resource. Independent validation is required to establish their biological and clinical significance. UMIN000040163.

title: Placental transcriptomes differ in human pregnancies complicated by severe fetal left heart obstruction.
abstract: The etiology of severe left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOL) of the heart, a common form of congenital heart disease (CHD), often remains unknown even after comprehensive genetic testing. Preclinical models implicate placental perturbations in abnormal cardiogenesis; however, little is known about connections between human placenta and fetal cardiac diseases. We profiled term placentas from severe LSOL pregnancies (n = 20) with and without placental pathologies and healthy controls (n = 10) to test whether severe fetal LSOL is associated with distinct transcriptomic and cellular states. Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues identified 1,030 differentially expressed protein-coding genes (580 [up], 450 [down]). Upregulated programs involved heart-valve development, endothelial signaling, and extracellular-matrix processes; while endocrine, trophoblast and gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling processes were downregulated. Severe LSOL pregnancies with histologically normal placentas showed enrichment of lymphatic-vascular development and cyclic-nucleotide signaling. Digital deconvolution analysis inferred reduced trophoblast fractions with reciprocal increase in endothelial and immune cell types. These findings support a unique placental gene expression in abnormal cardiac development, even in the absence of overt placental histopathology. These RNA expression signatures may serve as candidate biomarkers and lay the groundwork for mechanistic studies of the heart-placenta axis and future risk stratification in pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with severe LSOL.

title: Biomarkers Indicate Altered Outer Retinal Fluid Homeostasis in the Absence of Kv2.1/Kv8.2 Channels.
abstract: Photoreceptor Kv2.1/Kv8.2 voltage-gated potassium channels carry an outward potassium current, helping to set the resting membrane potential and to shape dim light responses. Because potassium flux in the outer retina influences extracellular osmolarity and fluid distribution, we hypothesized that Kv2.1/Kv8.2 channels also contribute to fluid homeostasis in this region of the retina. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging was performed in Kv8.2 heterozygous (Het) and knockout (KO) mice aged approximately 5 weeks under dark- and light-adapted conditions. Light-dark differences in the distance between the external limiting membrane (ELM) and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE; ΔELM-RPE) were calculated to quantify light-evoked outer retinal expansion, a biomarker associated with changes in subretinal space (SRS) fluid handling. As a secondary outcome, outer nuclear layer (ONL) thickness was also measured under both lighting conditions. Retinal gene expression was assessed by RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) and droplet digital RT-PCR. Retinal protein expression was determined by Western blotting and immunolabeling. ΔELM-RPE was significantly reduced in Kv8.2 KO mice compared with Het controls, indicating altered light-evoked outer retinal dynamics compatible with changes in SRS fluid handling. ONL thickness exhibited a small but significant light-dark change that was different between genotypes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed upregulation of osmosensitive genes, including osmolyte transporters and aquaporins. AQP1 protein expression in photoreceptors increased. These findings are consistent with altered outer retinal fluid homeostasis following loss of Kv8.2 and support a model in which photoreceptor potassium efflux contributes to osmotic water movement into the SRS.

title: Extracellular matrix stiffness kinetically stabilizes a cancer-associated state through a mechanochemical bistable switch.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma commonly develops in stiff, fibrotic livers, yet how extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics interact with intracellular feedback to stabilize persistent cancer-associated cell states remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether reciprocal coupling between integrin β1 (ITGB1) and the Yes-associated protein (YAP)/TEA domain transcription factor (TEAD) module can generate a stiffness-sensitive bistable regulatory circuit. Grade-stratified data from The Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma cohort showed positive ITGB1-YAP1 Spearman correlations with r-values of 0.626, 0.724, 0.664, and 0.727 for grades G1-G4, respectively. Public chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing profiles and loss-of-function experiments provided evidence consistent with reciprocal regulation in the proposed circuit. We formulated a bounded nonlinear model in which ECM stiffness modulates the ITGB1-to-YAP/TEAD arm. The model predicts a stiffness-sensitive onset of bistability near E⁎ ≈ 5.31 kPa at δ1 = 1.4; at the reference condition (δ1 = 1.5, E = 15 kPa), stable low- and high-activity states coexist with an intervening saddle. Consistent with the predicted stiffness sensitivity, stiffness-controlled polyacrylamide hydrogels spanning nominal elastic moduli of 0.1-80 kPa induced progressive increases in YAP nuclear localization and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine incorporation in LM3 and SNU-739 cells. On 15-kPa substrates, ITGB1-depleted LM3 cells showed lower mean YAP nuclear localization and CYR61/CTGF expression than nontargeting control small interfering RNA-transfected cells, consistent with ITGB1-dependent mechanotransduction. Perturbation of YAP or ITGB1 further reduced wound closure, three-dimensional growth, clonogenicity, and invasion. In the stochastic model, the high-state basin probability was 0.9977 at D = 0.008, and the H → L/L → H mean first-passage time ratio was 398; ratios above 104 occurred only at D ≲ 0.00491. Public single-cell RNA sequencing data provided compatible evidence of heterogeneous ITGB1 expression but lacked matched stiffness measurements. Together, these results support a mechanochemical framework in which ECM stiffness regulates an ITGB1-YAP/TEAD feedback circuit capable of model-predicted bistability and noise-dependent kinetic stabilization, while direct demonstration of hysteresis, an exact biological stiffness threshold, and physical switching times will require further experimental calibration and dynamic single-cell measurements.

title: Kmer-based reference-free assembly enables scalable and accurate single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
abstract: Single-cell RNA-seq typically depends on a high-quality reference genome, restricting its use in non-model organisms. De novo assembly offers a reference-free alternative, but conventional assemblers such as Trinity perform poorly on sparse, 3'-biased scRNA-seq data. We evaluated a k-mer-based, reference-free pipeline using RNA-Bloom, a multi-k-mer de Bruijn graph assembler optimized for single-cell data. Using a human breast cancer sample, we benchmarked RNA-Bloom and Trinity against the reference-based Cell Ranger pipeline (GRCh38) for assembly quality, expression quantification, cluster preservation, and automated cell-type annotation, and assessed scalability on ~ 18,000 cells. RNA-Bloom produced a less redundant, more contiguous transcriptome (N50 473 bp vs. 437 bp) with a higher TransRate score (0.45 vs. 0.41) and more efficient functional annotation. Although the RNA-Bloom expression matrix detected fewer genes per cell, it recapitulated cell population structure (ARI = 0.57, NMI = 0.68 vs. reference), and its annotations were concordant with the reference and cross-validated by SingleR, scmap, and scCATCH; Silhouette and MetaNeighbor analyses further supported cluster assessment.The pipeline scaled efficiently to 18,000 cells and generalized to a bovine (Bos taurus) dataset, achieving high annotation fidelity and recovery of major cell populations. These results establish k-mer-based reference-free assembly, particularly with RNA-Bloom, as a robust and accurate strategy for scRNA-seq analysis in reference-limited contexts.

title: Impaired cellular stress adaptability in Alzheimer's disease patient-derived fibroblasts: a PFKFB3-linked transcriptomic response to oxidative stress.
abstract: Aging-related impairment in cellular stress adaptability may contribute to vulnerability to Alzheimer's disease (AD), but patient-derived experimental models that preserve agingassociated molecular features remain underused. Here, we investigated transcriptomic responses to oxidative stress in ex vivo dermal fibroblasts derived from patients with AD and control participants matched for age and sex. Fibroblasts were exposed to hydrogen peroxide to induce reactive oxygen species-mediated stress, followed by RNA sequencing to identify disease-associated differences in stress-responsive gene regulation. AD-derived fibroblasts exhibited distinct oxidative stress response patterns, with altered regulation of pathways related to endoplasmic reticulum stress, immune activation, autophagy, protein synthesis, and cell cycle control. Systematic candidate gene prioritization identified PFKFB3 as a key stress-responsive gene showing reduced induction in AD fibroblasts. Lower PFKFB3 responsiveness was associated with poorer cognitive performance and higher levels of neurodegeneration-related blood biomarkers, including plasma pTau217, neurofilament light chain, and glial fibrillary acidic protein. In immortalized human astrocytes, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced cell viability under oxidative stress and altered transcriptional programs related to proteostasis, metabolic regulation, and immune activation. These findings suggest that AD is associated with impaired cellular stress adaptability in patient-derived fibroblasts and highlight PFKFB3 as a candidate node linking oxidative stress responsiveness, glial vulnerability, and AD-related pathological burden.

title: Gut dysbiosis-derived reduction in predicted short-chain fatty acid-producing capacity is associated with oxalate-induced renal oxidative stress involving the Sp3/SOD2 regulatory axis.
abstract: The gut microbiota and its metabolites, particularly short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), have been linked to kidney stones, but the specific molecular mechanisms by which they regulate kidney injury remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate these underlying molecular mechanisms. We analyzed gut microbiota diversity in a population, examined the expression of target genes and constructed dynamic expression profiles using a publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset, and investigated the interrelationships among the transcription factors Sp1, Sp3, and SOD2. Proximal tubular (PT) epithelial cells were treated with a combination of oxalate and SCFAs to assess the effects on cell viability and SOD2 expression. In the stone formers (SF) group, gut microbiota diversity and predicted SCFA-producing capacity were reduced, while predicted oxidative stress responses were enhanced. scRNA-seq revealed that during the transition of PT cells from a healthy to a stone-damaged state, SOD2, Sp1, Sp3, and SLC16A3 exhibited similar change trajectories. Sp3 expression was significantly positively correlated with SOD2, and in silico knockdown prediction indicated that Sp3 depletion may induce a significant downregulation of SOD2 expression. Preliminary cell experiments demonstrated that SCFAs may inhibit oxalate-induced damage to renal tubular epithelial cells by regulating SOD2 protein expression. This study suggests that in SF patients, the reduction in predicted SCFA-producing capacity caused by gut dysbiosis is associated with upregulation of SOD2 expression through Sp3-mediated transcriptional activation, a compensatory antioxidant response to oxalate-induced oxidative stress in PT cells. We therefore propose the following working hypothesis: the SCFA-Sp3-SOD2 axis may be involved in the "gut-kidney axis" mechanism underlying kidney stone formation; however, this requires direct measurement of SCFAs, verification of Sp3 binding to the SOD2 promoter, and confirmation in in vivo experiments.

title: M2 Macrophage-Derived Galectin-9 Enhances SLC1A5 Membrane Stability and Glutamine Metabolism to Promote Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally. Current therapeutic options remain limited by poor efficacy, and there is an urgent need to identify new therapeutic targets and strategies. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of HCC progression, and intercellular crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment (TME) critically shapes tumor cell metabolism. However, the cell types and mechanisms regulating HCC cell metabolism remain largely unclear. In this study, by combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomic data, we found that M2-like tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) were associated with highly metabolic HCC cells. Using intercellular protein interaction detection (ICPID), a proximity-labeling method developed in this study, we identified that Galectin-9 (Gal-9), highly expressed and secreted by M2 macrophages, is a ligand for the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 on HCC cells. This glycan-dependent interaction promoted the membrane localization of SLC1A5, thereby enhancing glutamine uptake and metabolism to promote HCC growth. Gal-9 neutralization or SLC1A5 inhibition suppressed glutamine metabolism and tumor-promoting phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo. Our study shows that M2 macrophage-derived Gal-9 can promote HCC progression by directly enhancing glutamine metabolism in HCC cells, and that the Gal-9-SLC1A5 axis may serve as a new therapeutic target for HCC treatment.

title: Neuropathology-defined Alzheimer's disease transcriptomic programs converge in blood at mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: BackgroundBlood transcriptomic studies in Alzheimer's disease (AD) often train signatures directly in blood, making it unclear whether signals reflect brain disease programs, blood-cell composition, or cohort structure.ObjectiveTo test how neuropathology-defined AD transcriptional programs appear in blood, whether distinct brain programs show a shared peripheral pattern, and whether that pattern is most evident during mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsThree directional gene sets were derived before blood analysis from postmortem brain RNA-seq (GSE278723) to represent amyloid-associated, neurodegeneration-related, and core AD changes. These brain-defined programs were projected into five whole-blood cohorts (1975 participants) using directional single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis and assessed for stage-specific patterns, comparison with size-matched random sets, sensitivity to estimated cell composition, dimensionality, held-out classification, and association with Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) genetic and fluid biomarkers.ResultsBrain-derived AD programs were detected across blood cohorts and showed a shared rather than separable pattern. Scores were highest at MCI, exceeded size-matched random baselines, and were not primarily explained by estimated blood-cell proportions. In GSE63060, P1/P2/P5 scores formed a dominant axis, with PC1 explaining 92.2% of directional half-score variance. A held-out classifier achieved AUC = 0.822, and ADNI analyses showed information beyond APOE ε4 and improved discrimination when blood scores were combined with cerebrospinal fluid pTau181/Aβ42.ConclusionsNeuropathology-defined AD transcriptomic programs form a shared peripheral axis that is most evident at MCI. This brain-anchored signal adds a systemic transcriptional dimension to genetic and fluid biomarkers and provides a biological framework for studying early AD-related disease in blood.

title: Malignant pleural effusion-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells promote lung cancer organoid proliferation via FGFR-MAPK/ERK pathway activation.
abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is often associated with poor prognosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Previous studies have shown that regulatory B cells (Bregs) can suppress the anti-tumor immune response in MPE, but the potential role of Bregs in promoting lung cancer and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Pleural effusion-derived organoids were successfully established from three of four patients with NSCLC and characterized by HE staining and IHC analyses. These organoids were co-cultured with sorted CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells isolated from malignant pleural effusion (MPE) or paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from the same patients. The formation efficiency of organoids and their proliferation status were evaluated through microscopic observation and EdU labeling detection. Mechanism exploration was conducted using RNA sequencing. Additionally, A549 cells were co-cultured with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells, and related signaling pathways were analyzed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. The FGFR inhibitor (infigratinib) was applied to verify the involvement mechanism of the MAPK/ERK pathway. Compared with the control group, MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells significantly promoted the proliferation of pleural effusion-derived organoids. Transcriptomic analysis showed enrichment of the MAPK signaling pathway in organoids co-cultured with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells. Consistently, in A549 cells, co-culture with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells significantly increased the protein expression of VEGFA, FGFR1-3, and p-ERK1/2, while total ERK1/2 remained unchanged. FGFR inhibition attenuated Breg-like cell-associated proliferation and reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation. These findings suggest that MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells are associated with enhanced lung cancer organoid proliferation and activation of the FGFR-MAPK/ERK pathway, with p-ERK1/2 emerging as an important downstream readout associated with this response. The FGFR-MAPK/ERK axis may represent a potential therapeutic target in the context of MPE-associated lung cancer.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies stem-like subpopulations and their gene signature in lung adenocarcinoma progression.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) demonstrates significant intra-tumor heterogeneity (ITH), which plays a critical role in disease progression and complicates therapeutic interventions. In the present study, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to analyze cellular populations derived from stage I and stage III LUAD tumors, alongside matched adjacent normal tissues, with the objective of delineating malignant cell states and identifying tumor-propagating subpopulations. Unsupervised clustering analysis identified eight principal cell lineages, with epithelial cells predominating within tumor samples. Notably, advanced-stage tumors demonstrated a shift toward an immunosuppressive microenvironment, characterized by elevated T cell exhaustion and an increased presence of pro-angiogenic macrophages. Further stratification of malignant cells revealed eleven distinct subclusters, with stage III tumors enriched for invasive and immunosuppressive phenotypes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis identified evolutionary transitions from alveolar-like states toward squamous and stress-responsive lineages. Employing CytoTRACE to evaluate stemness independently of predefined markers, we identified subpopulations of cancer stem cells (sub-CSCs) predominantly in stage III tumors. These sub-CSCs exhibited heightened transcriptional heterogeneity and a core gene signature associated with cytoskeletal motility, immune regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and protein homeostasis. A four-gene panel derived from this signature demonstrated robust prognostic significance in independent LUAD cohorts. Collectively, these findings enhance the current understanding of stemness-driven tumor progression in LUAD and suggest potential therapeutic targets to address tumor heterogeneity.

title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
abstract: Progression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome. Single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation. HSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903, respectively. Higher risk scores were associated with hypoxia, glycolysis, TGF-β/EMT signaling, stromal remodeling, and reduced adaptive immune programs. MK-2206 showed favorable predicted interactions with MIF and CXCL8, with greater modeled stability for the CXCL8 complex. Immunohistochemistry confirmed progressively increased CXCL8 and MIF expression from normal cervix to HSIL and SCC. Progression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

title: Fibroblast-derived MDK promotes Lymph node metastasis in Luminal Breast Cancer through an SDC4-USP9X-RELB deubiquitination axis.
abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is central to breast cancer staging and treatment decisions. Clinical observations indicate that luminal or hormone receptor-positive breast cancer may show a distinct clinical pattern of regional lymph node involvement, but the stromal and intracellular mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data, a multicenter institutional cohort, public single-cell RNA sequencing data, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Fibroblast states and candidate cell-cell communication pathways were examined using CytoTRACE, pseudotime, and ligand-receptor analyses. Functional and mechanistic validation included co-culture and Transwell assays, a mouse footpad-popliteal lymph node metastasis model, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, protein stability assays, and ubiquitination assays. Group comparisons used parametric or nonparametric tests, as appropriate. The SEER and multicenter cohorts showed a higher proportion of lymph node involvement in HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer than in the HER2-positive and triple-negative groups. Single-cell analysis identified a TINAGL1 + CAF population enriched in lymph node metastases, and spatial analysis demonstrated its proximity to epithelial tumor cells. Ligand-receptor analysis and tissue imaging supported MDK-SDC4 as a candidate stromal-tumor communication axis. Fibroblast-derived MDK promoted tumor-cell migration and invasion, and these responses were attenuated by SDC4 knockdown. Mechanistically, SDC4 associated with RELB and regulated its ubiquitination and proteasomal stability. USP9X associated with SDC4 and RELB, and USP9X perturbation altered RELB ubiquitination and protein stability. In vivo, SDC4 knockdown and overexpression produced opposite changes in imaging signals and popliteal lymph node volume, while RELB or USP9X knockdown attenuated the phenotype associated with SDC4 overexpression. Histological and immunohistochemical examination provided additional tissue-level characterization of the lymph node lesions. Fibroblast-derived MDK promotes breast cancer cell migration and invasion through tumor-cell SDC4. In vitro and in vivo findings support an SDC4-USP9X-RELB regulatory axis involving RELB ubiquitination and stability, providing mechanistic insight into stromal-tumor communication in regional lymph node metastasis.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals ANAPC1 overexpression and a potential TEAD4-associated regulatory relationship in cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CHOL) is a highly heterogeneous and aggressive malignancy that is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage because of the lack of early biomarkers, resulting in a poor prognosis. Although ANAPC1 overexpression has been reported in other cancers, its role and regulatory mechanisms in CHOL remain insufficiently characterized. To characterize ANAPC1 expression in CHOL, identify candidate upstream transcriptional regulators, and elucidate the associated functional programs and pathways. Multi-omics profiling was integrated with in-house immunohistochemical validation. Differential expression analyses, CRISPR-based functional screening, transcription-factor prioritization, ChIP-seq with epigenomic annotation, gene set enrichment analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell RNA-seq were conducted to investigate ANAPC1-associated regulatory mechanisms in CHOL.Structural modeling of predicted TEAD4-DNA complexes was additionally performed to assess the structural compatibility between TEAD4 and candidate ANAPC1 promoter motifs. ANAPC1 was significantly overexpressed in CHOL at both the transcriptomic level (436 CHOL vs. 213 non-CHOL samples) and the protein level (66 CHOL vs. 99 non-CHOL tissues), with spatial enrichment in cholangiocytes. Public CRISPR dependency screening indicated that ANAPC1 loss was associated with reduced cellular fitness in several CHOL cell lines, including HUCCT1. Integrative analyses identified TEAD4 as a candidate upstream regulator of ANAPC1, and TEAD4 was upregulated in CHOL. Public ChIP-seq and epigenomic datasets across multiple cell lines, including HUCCT1, HepG2, BE2-C, and MDA-MB-231, suggested TEAD4 occupancy at the ANAPC1 locus, together with active chromatin features such as H3K27ac signals near the promoter region. Across several bulk transcriptomic datasets, TEAD4 and ANAPC1 showed positive expression associations of varying magnitude, whereas spatial transcriptomics indicated partially overlapping regional enrichment within malignant areas.Protein-DNA complex modeling of a predicted candidate TEAD4-ANAPC1 promoter DNA complex yielded an ipTM score of 0.71 and a pTM score of 0.62 for the top-ranked candidate promoter motif. GSEA identified positive enrichment of proliferation- and RNA-processing-related pathways and negative enrichment of several immune-related pathways within the ANAPC1-correlated transcriptomic profile. Single-cell analysis further localized ANAPC1 expression mainly to cholangiocytes and identified a statistically significant but extremely weak cell-level correlation with TEAD4. These findings support the hypothesis of a putative TEAD4-ANAPC1 regulatory relationship in CHOL based on integrative epigenomic, transcriptomic, spatial, and structural analyses. Direct experimental validation is required to determine whether TEAD4 functionally regulates ANAPC1 transcription in cholangiocarcinoma.

title: Leucine-rich repeat neuronal protein 1 as a novel biomarker of breast cancer stem cells and poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer.
abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) play critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and disease relapse in breast cancer. Leucine-rich repeat neuronal protein-1 (LRRN1), previously identified as a regulator of pluripotency in human embryonic stem cells, has been implicated in oncogenic processes across multiple solid tumors. However, the functional role of LRRN1 in breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) and its clinical significance in breast cancer remain incompletely understood. LRRN1 expression was evaluated in breast cancer patient cohorts and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. BCSC-associated phenotypes were assessed by mammosphere formation, aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) activity, migration assay, orthotopic xenograft tumor growth, and extreme limiting dilution analysis (ELDA) to determine tumor-initiating cell (TIC) frequency following genetic manipulation of LRRN1 expression. AKT isoform expression was analyzed by quantitative RT-PCR and Western blotting. Transcriptomic alterations associated with LRRN1 silencing were examined using RNA sequencing followed by pathway-level analyses. Circulating anti-LRRN1 autoantibody levels were measured using a Luminex-based immunoassay and correlated with clinical outcomes. LRRN1 expression was significantly enriched in BCSCs compared with non-BCSC populations in PDX tumors. Genetic silencing of LRRN1 attenuated mammosphere formation, ALDH activity, migratory capacity, in vivo tumor growth, and tumor-initiating cell (TIC) frequency, whereas LRRN1 overexpression enhanced BCSC-associated properties across distinct breast cancer subtypes. At the molecular level, LRRN1 expression was associated with altered AKT isoform expression-most prominently AKT3-without detectable changes in AKT phosphorylation. RNA-seq analysis further revealed coordinated alterations in PI3K-AKT-related and cytoskeleton-associated signaling pathways following LRRN1 depletion. Clinically, elevated tumor LRRN1 mRNA expression and increased circulating anti-LRRN1 autoantibody levels were associated with poorer recurrence-free and overall survival, particularly in early-stage luminal breast cancer. Circulating anti-LRRN1 autoantibody titers positively correlated with tumor LRRN1 expression. LRRN1 is enriched in breast cancer stem cell populations and functionally contributes to CSC-related phenotypes, tumor-initiating capacity, and tumor growth. Its expression is linked to isoform-specific regulation of AKT and transcriptomic changes in AKT-related signaling pathways. Both tumor LRRN1 expression and the corresponding circulating autoantibody response may serve as prognostic biomarkers, highlighting the translational potential of LRRN1 for breast cancer risk stratification and therapeutic development.

title: Pathomics-based prediction of natural regulatory T cell infiltration in breast cancer.
abstract: Natural regulatory T cells (nTregs) are a key immunosuppressive component of the tumor microenvironment (TME), but their assessment typically requires specialized molecular assays. This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning-based pathomics model to predict nTregs infiltration directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images (WSI) of breast cancer and evaluate its prognostic significance. Data from 1097 breast cancer patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. A cohort of 928 patients with complete RNA-seq data was used to establish the prognostic value of nTregs (estimated by ImmuneCellAI). A subset of 791 patients with matched high-quality H&E-stained WSI was randomly split into training (n = 633) and validation (n = 158) cohorts. A total of 1488 quantitative pathomic features were extracted. After feature selection via minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) classifier was trained to predict high versus low nTregs status, generating a continuous Pathomics Score (PS). The PS was validated against FOXP3 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and evaluated for its association with overall survival (OS). Multi-omics analyses explored the underlying biology of PS-defined groups. High nTregs infiltration was an independent predictor of poor OS (HR = 1.58, 95% CI 1.10-2.28, p = 0.013). The GBM model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.81 (95% CI 0.78-0.85) in the training cohort and 0.72 (95% CI 0.63-0.80) in the validation cohort. The PS showed a strong correlation with FOXP3+ cell density (p < 0.001) and was independently associated with worse OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.15-2.46, p = 0.008). Patients with high PS exhibited a distinct transcriptomic signature enriched for immune activation pathways (e.g., estrogen responses) and upregulated immune checkpoint genes (e.g., CD276, TNFSF4, TNFSF9), alongside an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by increased nTregs and M2-like macrophage estimates. We developed and validated a pathomics model that non-invasively predicts nTregs infiltration and patient prognosis from standard H&E images. The PS serves as a novel, accessible digital biomarker that captures the complexity of an inflamed yet immunosuppressive TME and has the potential to augment clinical decision-making, particularly in resource-limited settings.

title: Aging-Related Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Immune Heterogeneity in Tuberculosis: An Exploratory Multi-Cohort Analysis.
abstract: Aging-related genes (ARGs) may contribute to immune heterogeneity in tuberculosis (TB), but their diagnostic and biological relevance remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify TB-associated ARG transcripts, characterize their immune and molecular correlates, and evaluate their exploratory diagnostic performance across prespecified cohorts. Public TB transcriptomic cohorts were analyzed together with a local bulk RNA-seq cohort comprising 5 TB patients and 5 controls and a local single-cell RNA-seq cohort comprising 3 active TB patients and 3 controls. The local cohorts were selected using random sampling. Age-adjusted differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, immune-infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, single-cell annotation, and Comparative Toxicogenomics Database-based compound-gene screening were performed. GSE83456 included 45 TB patients and 61 controls. Age-adjusted differential expression identified 189 differentially expressed genes, and the intersection of DEGs, ARGs, and blue-module genes yielded 11 discovery candidates. Nested model selection in GSE83456 identified a naive Bayes classifier based on STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14. Across five repeated stratified nested cross-validation runs, the mean AUC was 0.962, with a repeat-level range of 0.954-0.969. Balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 0.926, 0.911, 0.941, and 0.928, respectively. Exploratory evaluations included GSE19439, GSE34608, GSE62525, GSE19444, and the local RNA-seq cohort. Consensus clustering separated TB samples into two ARG-associated subgroups with distinct immune-infiltration and pathway-activity profiles. CIBERSORT analysis identified significant TB-control differences in 9 of 22 inferred immune-cell types. Single-cell analysis demonstrated heterogeneous expression of STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 across annotated immune-cell subsets. CTD screening generated exploratory compound-gene associations that provide testable hypotheses for future experimental studies. Age-adjusted multi-cohort analysis identified candidate ARG-associated TB markers and immune patterns. STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 are candidate markers rather than clinically validated biomarkers and require independent experimental and clinical validation.
